memory_lessons.applicability: These are full-call search measurements for the same recursive reduction workload; they do not isolate kernel cost or confirm a final result.
memory_lessons.claim: The two measured hand-written shuffle variants were correct on 10 cases and averaged 30.6225 and 30.8038 microseconds, compared with 46.4832 microseconds for the measured baseline. Neither result is a confirmation.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Build and validate the CUB variant, then compare repeated full-call measurements under the same protocol and request confirmation if selected.

proposal.hypothesis: CUB's BLOCK_REDUCE_WARP_REDUCTIONS may lower the intra-block synchronization and reduction overhead compared with both the baseline modulo/shared-memory tree and the hand-written shuffle variants, while keeping the 128-thread, one-element-per-lane mapping and recursive ceil(count/128) passes. Signed 64-bit accumulation and ping-pong scratch partials avoid intermediate int overflow; only the final block writes int. The hand-written variants measured 30.6225 and 30.8038 microseconds versus the baseline's 46.4832 microseconds, but those search measurements neither isolate the reduction primitive nor establish a CUB speedup.

retained: Replace the modulo/shared-memory reduction tree with cub::BlockReduce<long long, 128, cub::BLOCK_REDUCE_WARP_REDUCTIONS>::Sum, keeping 128 threads and one input element per lane.
Accumulate all block partials in signed 64-bit values, ping-pong them through compact caller-provided scratch buffers, and narrow to int only for the final reduction output.
Retain recursive ceil(count/128) passes, default-stream kernel launches, and the final asynchronous device-to-device copy.
